prompt.context: Rock Energy is an Oil & Gas company evaluating the purchase of rights to extract oil from one of three oil fields in Latin America. After purchasing the rights to extract oil from one of these fields, Rock Energy will outsource the drilling activity.
prompt.question: How would you evaluate the three oil fields, and which oil field should Rock Energy purchase?

clarifying_info.q: How long do the drilling rights last, and when does production begin?
clarifying_info.a: The rights give Rock Energy the right to drill during year 1 and produce oil for 20 years. Assume no oil is produced until the beginning of year 2.

clarifying_info.q: How many drilling rigs can be deployed per region?
clarifying_info.a: Rock Energy can get the drilling operator to deploy a maximum of 10 rigs in each region.

clarifying_info.q: What does the rig day cost include?
clarifying_info.a: The cost of the rig day includes crew, consumables, and services.
Any amount of oil extracted will be sold at the current spot market price.

clarifying_info.q: Are there maintenance costs during the production years?
clarifying_info.a: For simplicity, assume the oil wells will produce the same amount of oil for the next 20 years with no maintenance costs.

clarifying_info.q: What is the upfront cost to acquire the rights?
clarifying_info.a: The rights to extract oil cost $40M in each region.

exhibits.title: Oil Field Profiles, 2010
exhibits.shows: A comparison table of three regions showing drilling rates (meters/day), average well depth (meters), number of rigs that would operate, average well production (barrels per day), and cost per rig day. A footnote explains that wells are continuously dug for one year only, then oil is extracted going forward, and rigs move to a new well once the current one is complete.

framework: Determine drilling time per well per region (depth / penetration rate)
Calculate cost per well (days to complete x cost per rig day)
Estimate annual well production (barrels per day x 360 days)
Calculate yearly revenue per well (spot price x barrels per year)
Derive profit per well (revenue minus cost per well)
Calculate number of wells drillable per year (360 / drilling days x 10 rigs)
Calculate total revenue, total cost (including $40M rights fee), and total profit per region
Compare regions and identify best investment
Discuss qualitative risks and other factors that could affect the decision

questions.prompt: How many days does it take to drill one well in each region?
questions.guidance: Candidate divides average well depth by drilling penetration rate. Region 1: 1200/20=60 days. Region 2: 2700/30=90 days. Region 3: 3600/20=180 days.

math.setup: Days to drill = Average depth (meters) / Drilling rate (meters per day)
math.answer: Region 1 = 60 days, Region 2 = 90 days, Region 3 = 180 days

questions.prompt: What is the cost to drill one well in each region?
questions.guidance: Candidate multiplies days to complete one well by the daily rig cost.

math.setup: Cost per well = Days to complete well x Cost per rig day

questions.prompt: What is the annual oil production per well and the annual revenue per well, given a spot price of $50/barrel?
questions.guidance: Annual production = barrels per day x 360 days. Revenue per well = production x spot price.

math.setup: Production per well per year = daily production x 360. Revenue per well = production x $50.
steps: Region 1 production: 100 x 360 = 36,000 barrels; revenue = 36,000 x $50 = $1,800,000
Region 2 production: 200 x 360 = 72,000 barrels; revenue = 72,000 x $50 = $3,600,000
Region 3 production: 300 x 360 = 108,000 barrels; revenue = 108,000 x $50 = $5,400,000

questions.prompt: What is the profit per well and profit margin per well for each region?
questions.guidance: Profit per well = Revenue per well minus cost per well. Margin = profit / cost per well.

math.setup: Profit per well = Yearly revenue per well - Cost per well. Margin = Profit per well / Cost per well.
math.answer: Region 1 = $1.5M profit/well (500% margin); Region 2 = $2.7M profit/well (300% margin); Region 3 = $1.8M profit/well (50% margin)

questions.prompt: How many wells can be drilled in one year per region with 10 rigs, and what is the total profit per region?
questions.guidance: Number of wells = (360 / days per well) x 10 rigs. Total revenue = revenue per well x wells. Total cost = (cost per well x wells) + $40M rights. Profit = total revenue - total cost. The key insight is that Region 1's high per-well margin is offset by drilling fewer wells per year relative to total fixed cost; Region 2 yields the best total profit.

math.setup: Wells per year = (360 / drilling days) x 10 rigs. Total revenue = yearly revenue per well x wells. Total cost = cost per well x wells + $40M. Profit = total revenue - total cost.

brainstorming.prompt: Even though the numbers make Region 2 the best investment, what other qualitative issues would Rock Energy need to consider before finalizing the decision?

categories.name: Political & Regulatory Risk
ideas: Political stability of the region could affect access to well sites

categories.name: Cost & Insurance
ideas: Insurance costs may differ significantly by country based on local regulations
Liability caps vary by country, affecting required insurance coverage
Labor contracts and union agreements may affect operational costs

categories.name: Commodity & Market Risk
ideas: Volatility of oil prices: prices below $27/barrel would make all regions unprofitable
Oil quality differences across regions could affect the realized spot price
Long 20-year production horizon exposes Rock Energy to significant price swings

categories.name: Operational Risk
ideas: Uncertainty around actual barrels extracted per day vs. projected

recommendation: Rock Energy should invest in buying the rights for Region 2, which yields the highest total annual profit of $68M

Although Region 1 has the highest per-well profit margin (500% vs 300%), Region 2's higher production per well and faster drilling pace generates significantly more total revenue, more than offsetting its higher per-well costs and the fixed $40M rights fee
risks: Oil price volatility: if prices fall below approximately $27/barrel, all regions show negative returns
Political instability in the Latin American region selected could disrupt operations
Actual well production may differ from projected 200 barrels/day
Insurance and regulatory requirements could add unanticipated costs
next_steps: Conduct an expected value analysis assigning probabilities to different barrels-per-day outcomes to stress-test the recommendation
Assess political risk and insurance cost profiles for the specific country of Region 2
Review local labor contracts and union agreements before finalizing the investment
